title: Implementation discipline
summary: Implementation MUST remain within the approved plan, establish exactly one deterministic pre-edit repository-check baseline per unit of work, run only blast-radius tests while iterating and the fast profile once as final validation, and directly remediate every cause of a retry.
instructions: Each material change MUST map to an acceptance criterion or an explicitly documented enabling change.
Agents MUST NOT redesign adjacent systems unless the approved plan requires it.

Before the first coder invocation of a unit of work, the harness MUST run and persist exactly one baseline for each interior gate profile. An interior gate profile is a profile other than full that a source-allowed stage gate references under the run's verification level. Under every built-in level the interior gate profiles are static and fast. The full profile MUST NOT run as a baseline. The baseline makes a pre-existing failure distinguishable from a regression.

A unit of work is one delivery run, or one cohort session together with every chunk run and the release run it starts. A cohort session MUST hold exactly one shared baseline per interior gate profile. The first run of the session that prepares a source-allowed stage captures it in its own worktree. That run records it on the cohort record under runtime/logs/cohorts/. Every other run of the session MUST adopt the recorded baseline and MUST NOT capture its own.

The coder MUST inspect the pre-implementation static and fast baselines before editing. The coder SHOULD repair existing failures when repair is bounded and low-risk. An unchanged pre-existing failure MUST NOT block the workflow when remediation would be broad, structural, or unrelated to the approved change. Any new or worsened diagnostic MUST remain a hard failure.

On a retry of the implementation stage, the coder MUST do work that directly addresses every issue causing the retry. The coder MUST populate implementation.remediation with cause, action, and evidence. A paperwork-only retry is prohibited.

After each group of changes, the coder SHOULD run the impacted iteration profile plus every test it added. In self-development that profile is `pan tests impacted`, which selects modules by static import-graph analysis. In a target installation the coder MUST use the target's declared impacted profile. Only when no impacted profile exists, the coder MUST select the tests in the immediate blast radius by judgment. Every test command MUST derive from runtime/repository-checks.json or the target's documented test entry points, and the coder MUST NOT guess a test command. The coder MAY run the static profile freely.

The impacted mapping does not reach every changed path. When a changed path yields no impacted test, the coder MUST choose a judgment cohort of tests that cover that path. The coder MUST NOT treat the empty selection as an absent blast radius. It MUST record each unreached path and its chosen cohort. Cohort selection is judgment-only and carries no deterministic check.
Each added test MUST appear in tests_added with the contract it proves.

When the coder believes the change is complete, it MUST run the fast profile once as the final validation. The coder MUST NOT run the fast profile at any other point and MUST NOT run it a second time. After a failure of that run, the coder MUST fix the cause. The coder MUST then re-run only the impacted selection, the failing tests, and every test it added. Every other test execution MUST be the impacted profile plus the tests the coder added. The coder MUST NOT substitute its own estimate of the blast radius for the impacted selection.
On a retry that changed only output claims or evidence, the coder MUST NOT run any test profile. The retry MUST cite the evidence of the prior run.

The harness MUST rerun declared deterministic gates independently on any submission that can still succeed. The next instruction names the one exception: an accepted recorded pass. A non-success outcome is a declared failure or blocked result, a failed hard self-criterion, or a failed read attestation. When the submitted output already decides a non-success outcome, the harness MUST NOT run shell gate commands. The harness MUST record each affected gate as skipped with the deciding reason.

The harness MAY accept a recorded clean pass of the identical gate command instead of re-executing it. Acceptance needs an unchanged Git workspace fingerprint, an unchanged repository-check configuration, a record under 24 hours old, and a resolved run baseline. The harness MUST mark an accepted pass as cached. An accepted pass MUST carry the original captured output as its evidence. An accepted pass MUST NOT be a failure, timeout, skip, override, or baseline-relative credit. PAN_GATE_CACHE=0 disables acceptance.

Before submission, the implementation record, changed-file claims, retry-remediation evidence, acceptance evidence, and referenced summary artifact MUST run their resolved policy-bound validators under VALID-001.

The fast/default profile MUST contain only deterministic offline tests. The coder MUST mark tests that make real external network or catalog calls, and MUST confine them to a secondary, integration, or full-only profile.

A repository-check gate MAY classify a new failing test as `environment_or_flake` only under three conditions. First, the test is outside the changed import closure. Second, the baseline did not fail that identity. Third, exactly one isolated rerun through the profile's reviewed `isolation_command` exits cleanly and reports the named test as run. The changed closure MUST come from the dirty working tree together with the paths the stage absorbed into a commit. When no change evidence exists at all, the gate MUST classify every failure as `isolation_unavailable` and MUST NOT reclassify.

A clean exit whose transcript does not name the test MUST classify as `isolation_unproven` and MUST fail the gate. A failure inside the closure, a second failure, an unparseable identity, or an absent isolation command MUST fail as before. The harness MUST record each classification, and its reason, in the deterministic gate result. `loadRepositoryChecks` validates that `isolation_command` contains `{file}` and either `{test_pattern}` or `{test}`. `{test_pattern}` receives the test name as an anchored regular expression, and `{test}` receives it literally. This instruction is the implementation specification until repository-check configuration becomes a policy-bound registry target.

Elapsed clock time alone MUST NOT fail a repository check that exits successfully. The harness MUST record a slow successful check as an operator FYI. A timeout, hang, nonzero exit, or new diagnostic remains actionable.
